newsitem.title: UK: Rostelekom to keep control of firm - FT.
newsitem.headline: Rostelekom to keep control of firm - FT.

text.p: Russian national phone company Rostelekom will retain full operational control of its business despite the transfer of a major stake in the firm, the Financial Times reported on Wednesday.
Rostelekom president Oleg Belov was quoted as saying the transfer of the stake to Svyazinvest would not alter the way it was run or disadvantage the company's other shareholders.

As a result of the transfer, Svyazinvest, a telecoms holding company, would take control of the state's shareholding in Rostelekom, speaking for 51 percent of the company's voting rights, the Financial Times said.
"The transfer of the state shareholding to Svyazinvest does not make a difference for the management of Rostelekom," Belov told the paper in an interview.
He said there was no question of a full merger between the two companies.
The transfer has cast a shadow over Rostelekom's share price recently, with some analysts questioning the company's direction under Svyazinvest.
Belov said Rostelekom planned to invest about $400 million in upgrading its telephone network this year, and was also working on plans to set up an American Depositary Receipt (ADR) programme.
The report said the company planned to raise substantial amounts of capital via a eurobond issue, although details were unclear.
